solutionSql: SELECT s.id, s.customer_id, s.weight_kg FROM shipments AS s WHERE s.id BETWEEN 1 AND 40 AND s.weight_kg > (SELECT AVG(o.weight_kg) FROM shipments AS o WHERE o.customer_id = s.customer_id) ORDER BY s.id;

rules.howSolved: A correlated subquery averages over o.customer_id = s.customer_id.
The comparison is weight_kg > AVG(...), the mean, not a MAX.
AVG skips NULL weights; a shipment with a NULL weight_kg gives a NULL comparison and is not returned.

ambiguities: 'the average weight_kg of all shipments with the same customer_id' is read as every shipment for that customer in the whole table. The phrase 'For shipments with ids 1 through 40' is read as limiting only the returned rows, not the population of the average.
'including the shipment itself' is read as the shipment counting in its own customer's average. The query does this, but the rules list does not declare it.
notes: Read-only item. Ran without error on sample, nulls and boundary. The scope reading of the average is the main interpretive choice; the alternative (average restricted to ids 1 to 40) would change the result. Solve time is an estimate.
